title: Random coordinate frames and partial permutation laws
main_claim: Thorp shuffle on n=2^d cards: worst-start TV distance after 32800d physical shuffles tends to 0 as d→∞ (Thm 1.1). The paper also claims 2048d and 512d variants, the 512d one relying on a companion paper.
coverage: I checked the full proof chain for Thm 1.1 (Sections 1–6). (1) Frame identity, Lemma 2.1: the column update L_t=L_{t-1}(I+e_{i(t)}c_t) does give L_{t-1}e_{i(t)}=v_t via recurrence (2.2); L_tL_{t-1}^{-1}=I+v_t f_t with f_t(v_t)=0 lies in C_{v_t}; and the telescoping holds. R^{-T}=I because T=1025d. (2) Online energy: the direction factorization is valid because the schedule is generated independently of the coins. The exact decrement (average vs transport) and the bipartite identity hold, the latter with +2(ΣD0 z)^2 since Σz=0. Cross pairs across a linear hyperplane have probability 2/n, giving a loss of at least min(u,w)/n·Δ. (3) Balance: Z_t(M_a)⊆D_t^j; given the history, Z_t(M_a) is a uniform m-subset. E3^X≤2^m gives b_n=2(2/3^{3/4})^m, and the event B_t is F_t-measurable, so the recurrence (1-γ)EΔ+γP(B) is valid. With α=1/256 and 1024d steps, the decay is ≤e^{-4d}. The sequential TV/Cauchy–Schwarz tuple bound gives ≤ n^{3/2}/2·sqrt(e^{-4d}+b_n)→0, since 1.5 ln2<2. (4) Cosets: the complement-image identification with left cosets gH_a is right. Trimming gives ε≤2δ and caps 2/(1-ε)≤4. (5) Orbit span: the dim W_a ≤ Σ_{dim≤D^{1/k}} dim^2 bound holds, using End(V_π) acting on V_π⊗A. The coset-constant projection comparison, the Schur average dim W/D, and Cauchy–Schwarz over the orthogonal E_a all check. (6) Tableau lemma: all three classes check. Class 1: 2·2^{-15h}. Class 2: subdiagram plus central binomial, (s+1)^16 2^{-s}. Class 3: ≤2L-1 diagonals, product of factorials ≥2^{3s/4}, 2^{-11s}. Together they cover every non-row/column shape. (7) Completion: the exponent (1-18/64)/2=23/64 is right. With ℓ=32 the bound is D·D·A^64·D^{-23}=A^64 D^{-21}, summable to o(1) over non-trivial, non-sign irreps. The fair-sign argument works by flipping one last-step bit. The Plancherel normalization is correct, and 32·1025d=32800d. Not audited: Sections 7–11 (the 2048d orbit-transfer theorem, the 512d corollary relying on the companion, and the frame variants / character sections).
sibling_notes: The main theorem does not depend on the companions: it is proved without the Fourier companion or the deterministic-coordinate (1600d) companion. Siblings in family 238 also report no_gap_found for the companions. Only the 512d corollary (Sec 7c) imports the companion isotypic estimate, and I did not audit it.
